title: Process for preparation of mesotrione and its intermediates
abstract: The present disclosure provides a new and improved process for preparation of intermediate compounds and synthesis of mesotrione therefrom. The present disclosure provides an economical, efficient and eco-friendly process for preparation of mesotrione.
patent_summary: The document discloses a three-step process for preparing the herbicide mesotrione of formula (I) from 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV): oxidation of NMST to 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with an oxidant, sodium hypochlorite in the worked examples, in the presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide as catalyst; direct coupling of NMSBA with 1,3-cyclohexanedione using N,N'-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide in a chlorinated solvent, preferably dichloromethane, to give the enol ester of formula (II); and conversion of that enol ester to mesotrione with sodium cyanide in the presence of an organic base, preferably triethylamine, and a solvent. Separate independent claims are directed to the oxidation and to the coupling as preparations of the two intermediates in their own right, and to the two-step route from NMST to the enol ester, and the description states that the whole sequence may be run in one and the same reaction vessel without isolating either intermediate.
novelty_claims: The background at [0010] objects that the known routes "involve tedious procedures, e.g. a relatively greater number of steps, which includes conversion of NMSBA to NMSBC, as well as isolation and purification of intermediates at each step", and that they "involve use of high amount of solvents that leads to production of high volume of effluent". The contribution positioned against that is the direct coupling of claim 7, "a process for preparation of an enol ester of formula (II) by reaction of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione", which [0036] says "does not require the additional step of converting NMSBA to an intermediate of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoyl chloride (NMSBC)", so the disclosed route reaches mesotrione without ever forming the acid chloride that the US 7,820,863 process of [005] passes through; alongside it stands the oxidation of claims 5 and 6, NMST oxidised "using sodium hypochlorite in presence of ruthenium oxide", where the cited US 5,591,890, US5424481, CN105669504A and CN106565561A oxidations use a cobalt or vanadium catalyst with acetic, sulfuric or nitric acid, and where [0033] adds that the ruthenium oxide is recovered by filtration and reused. The abstract's "economical, efficient and eco-friendly" and the objects at [0013] and [0014] are stated aims rather than demonstrated effects: the document contains no comparative example and no data measured against any cited process, and the figures it gives for the coupling (yield "at least 65%", purity "at least 85%", solvent recovery of ">85%") are specification minima with no prior-art counterpart printed beside them.
